report.answer_text:
On April 2, 2025, which President Trump called “Liberation Day,” the U.S. announced two tiers of new import tariffs under Executive Order 14257: (whitehouse.gov)
A 10% baseline tariff on most U.S. goods imports, effective April 5, 2025. (whitehouse.gov)
Higher “reciprocal” tariffs for dozens of trading partners, originally scheduled for April 9, 2025. These rates replaced the 10% baseline for those partners; they were not added on top of it. (whitehouse.gov)
| Trading partner | Rate announced April 2 |
|---|---:|
| European Union | 20% |
| Japan | 24% |
| South Korea | 25% |
| India | 26% |
| Taiwan | 32% |
| China | 34% |
| Vietnam | 46% |
| Cambodia | 49% |
| Lesotho | 50% |
The full list was published in Annex I of the order. Canada and Mexico remained under separate tariff rules, and the new tariffs excluded certain goods, including pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, and steel, aluminum, and autos already subject to separate sectoral tariffs. (whitehouse.gov)
These were the originally announced rates. China’s rate was raised before the scheduled April 9 start, and most other higher rates were paused effective April 10, leaving the 10% baseline in place for most partners. (usitc.gov)

quotes.text: (a) Except as otherwise provided in this order, all articles imported into the customs territory of the United States shall be, consistent with law, subject to an additional ad valorem rate of duty of 10 percent.
Such rates of duty shall apply with respect to goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m.
eastern daylight time on April 5, 2025, except that goods loaded onto a vessel at the port of loading

pages.page_reason: The page states that an additional 10 percent ad valorem duty applies to all articles imported into the U.S. with rates applying to goods entered on or after 12:01 a.m. EDT on April 5, 2025, subject to exceptions, which supports the claim that the 10% baseline applied to most imports effective April 5, 2025.
